items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: Greg Cosell evaluates Caleb Williams' progression going into his third season as highly positive, praising his pure throwing talent but noting a need to play more strictly within the offense's structure when it works.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: There are few guys that throw as beautiful a ball as Caleb Williams, so there's no concerns about the talent level... I would say he's right on track.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.topic: Multiple TE usage under Ben Johnson
items.summary: Cosell notes Chicago's draft choice of tight end Sam Roush suggests a shift towards heavier tight end packages (12 and 13 personnel) under Ben Johnson to ease the burden on Caleb Williams.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: I'm fascinated to see if Ben Johnson decides to go a lot more with multiple tight end personnel packages, including 13 personnel with three tight ends.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: The Lions reshuffled their offensive line, moving Penei Sewell to left tackle, inserting draft pick Blake Miller at right tackle, and bringing in Cade Mays from Carolina to play center.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: They moved Sewell to left tackle, which is what he played in college... Blake Miller, they drafted, is going to step in at right tackle.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: Ross Tucker points out that both projected starting safeties for the Lions, Brian Branch and Kirby Joseph, are returning from injuries, which introduces volatility to their secondary.
items.speaker: Ross Tucker
items.quote: Both safeties, Branch and Joseph, are coming off injury. The whole Kirby Joseph health situation has been a little bit interesting.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: Greg Cosell discusses the transition to new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, highlighting Gannon's signature 5-across look-ahead zone principles that hide safety/corner run defense assignments.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: I'm curious to see how Gannon deploys them. He did some really interesting things in Arizona where he basically lined up in like a lot of five-across looks.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: Greg Cosell maintains a skeptical view of JJ McCarthy's long-term projection, pointing out that his college film concerns have manifested as mechanical and health issues in the pros.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: I did not view him as a first-round pick. Obviously, the Vikings did. It hasn't worked out for a number of reasons, some of which I felt like I saw on tape when I watched him in college.

items.episode_title: Greg Cosell: 2026 NFC North Season PREVIEW
items.summary: The Vikings' acquisition of Kyler Murray means adjusting Kevin O'Connell's highly structured, timing-based Shanahan-McVay offense to account for Murray's off-schedule creation.
items.speaker: Greg Cosell
items.quote: Kevin O'Connell comes from the Kyle Shanahan, Sean McVay school of offense, which is really highly choreographed... This is going to be different for him, and it's something he's going to have to learn.

items.episode_title: NFL Injury Expert Dr. David Chao On The Major NFL Injury Storylines
items.summary: Dr. Chao believes Mahomes' recovery will be treated conservatively. He would play if it were the Super Bowl, but the Chiefs are expected to sit him early in the season.
items.speaker: Dr. David Chao
items.quote: If week one were the Super Bowl, guarantee, book it, Patrick Mahomes would play and start that game. But it's not the Super Bowl... I see them being conservative.

items.episode_title: NFL Injury Expert Dr. David Chao On The Major NFL Injury Storylines
items.summary: Dr. Chao flags Micah Parsons as a candidate to start on the PUP list and have a delayed return to play, contrasting with Mahomes' timeline due to positional demands.
items.speaker: Dr. David Chao
items.quote: We fully expect him to start on PUP, and we don't expect him to come off PUP as soon as he's eligible. I think it's mid-to-late season before he returns.

items.episode_title: NFL Injury Expert Dr. David Chao On The Major NFL Injury Storylines
items.summary: Dr. Chao states Tyreek Hill will likely not play this season because of his devastating multi-ligament knee injury and financial insurance incentives.
items.speaker: Dr. David Chao
items.quote: Tyreek Hill, I've said all along, he's not playing this season. It's a multi-ligament injury... and at age 32, why would he?

items.episode_title: NFL Injury Expert Dr. David Chao On The Major NFL Injury Storylines
items.summary: Dr. Chao highlights major injury concerns in Atlanta's quarterback room, pointing out Michael Penix's extensive surgical history and Tua's high vulnerability to concussions.
items.speaker: Dr. David Chao
items.quote: They play a position that is very prone to injury... Michael Penix has had a number of injuries that are season ending... Tua, if he were to get another concussion, it probably wouldn't be a one-week sit-out.

items.episode_title: NFL Injury Expert Dr. David Chao On The Major NFL Injury Storylines
items.summary: Dr. Chao notes that large defensive tackles like Caleb Banks face recurring foot fractures because modern athletic development adds muscle power without increasing bone/tendon thickness.
items.speaker: Dr. David Chao
items.quote: Caleb Banks... had multiple fractures of his metatarsal... The plug means there's long-term articular cartilage issues... It's a concern.

items.topic: Dr. Chao's SIC Score injury database
items.summary: Fezik highly praises the Dr. Chao group's SIC Score database for tracking team injuries (offensive line, defensive line, etc.), noting that their core injury model has hit 56.5% over the last seven years.

items.quote: Love the concept that they have... they have their SIC score for all the teams, and yes it's obvious when it's the quarterback, but it's not obvious sometimes with cluster injuries on the O-line, etc.

items.quote: If you're not betting over a hundred dollars a game... don't be buying picks because the cost of the picks is too onerous.
